spots.name: Vorontsov Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Vorontsov Palace or the Alupka Palace is a historic palace situated at the foot of the Crimean Mountains near the town of Alupka in Crimea. The Vorontsov Palace is one of the oldest and largest palaces in Crimea, and has been one of the most popular tourist attractions on Crimea's southern coast.

spots.name: Swallow's Nest
spots.summary: The Swallow's Nest is a decorative castle located at Gaspra, a small spa town between Yalta and Alupka on the Crimean peninsula.

spots.name: Artek
spots.summary: Artek is an international children's center on the Black Sea in the town of Gurzuf located on the Crimean Peninsula, near Ayu-Dag. It was established on 16 June 1925 as the V. I. Lenin All-Union Pioneer Camp.

photo.author: International Children's Camp "Artek", traced in SVG by C records

spots.name: Juma-Jami Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Juma-Jami Mosque, also known as the Friday Mosque, is located in Yevpatoria, Crimea. Built between 1552 and 1564, it is a mosque designed by the Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan.

names.ja: イェウパトーリヤの金曜モスク

spots.name: Foros Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of Christ's Resurrection is a popular tourist attraction close to the southernmost tip of the Crimea, known primarily for its scenic location, overlooking the Black Sea littoral from a 400-metre cliff near Baidarsky Pass.

names.fr: Église de la Résurrection-du-Christ de Foros
names.es: Iglesia de la Resurrección de Cristo

spots.name: Yusupov Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Yusupov Palace is a palace located in the town of Koreiz, near Yalta in Crimea. It was built for Prince Felix Yusupov-Soumorokov-Elston and his wife Princess Zinaida Yusupova (1861–1939) in 1909 by Nikolay Krasnov, the architect responsible for the imperial Livadia Palace in nearby Yalta.

spots.name: Dulber

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Dulber Palace is a Moorish Revival palace designed by Nikolay Krasnov in Koreiz, near Yalta in Crimea.

spots.name: Donuzlav
spots.summary: Lake Donuzlav, also referred to as Donuzlav Bay, is the deepest lake of Crimea and biggest in Chornomorske Raion. It is a protected landscape and recreational park of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea.

spots.name: Eupatorian Kenassas

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Eupatorian Kenassas is a complex of Karaite Jewish synagogues located on Karaimskaya Street in Yevpatoria, Crimea, Ukraine. The synagogue complex is the oldest active Karaite synagogue in the world.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Mangup
spots.summary: Mangup also known as Mangup Kale is a historic fortress in Crimea, located on a plateau about 13 kilometres east of Sevastopol.

spots.name: Eski-Kermen
spots.summary: Eski-Kermen or Eski Kermen was a cave town and fortress in the Crimea in the south of Ukraine. Founded by the Byzantine Empire in the 6th century to defend against the Göktürks, it was conquered by the Khazars in the 7th or 8th century.

spots.name: Mount Kosh-Kaya
spots.summary: Mount Koshka is a mountain in the Crimean Mountains near the settlement of Simeiz within the Greater Yalta metropolitan area. The original name in the Crimean Tatar language means "double rock", while the Russian name means "cat", as the shape of the mountain resembles a lying cat. The height is 254 metres.
